mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes during a tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes with INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent surge in both personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their 6-month moving averages signals a robust demand recovery, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 70% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the labor force participation rate (implied by inverse of UNRATE dynamics) above 63% for six consecutive months signals a tightening labor market, which supports wage growth and boosts consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained low unemployment (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for at least two consecutive quarters signals strengthening consumer demand, which lifts corporate revenues and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
